title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations for Trillion-Parameter Models
hook: Data-parallel training wastes memory by copying optimizer states, gradients, and parameters onto every GPU. ZeRO partitions them instead — fitting 100B+ parameter models.
key_points: Partitions optimizer states, gradients, and parameters across data-parallel GPUs instead of replicating them.
Trained 100B+ parameter models on 400 GPUs at about 15 PetaFLOPs.
An 8x increase in model size and 10x in performance over the prior state of the art.
Runs up to 13B-parameter models with no model parallelism; powers 17B-parameter Turing-NLG.
content_html: Samyam Rajbhandari, Jeff Rasley, Olatunji Ruwase, and Yuxiong He at Microsoft introduced the Zero Redundancy Optimizer, or ZeRO, to attack the memory waste in data-parallel training. Standard data parallelism keeps a full copy of the optimizer states, gradients, and parameters on every GPU; ZeRO partitions them across workers instead. With it they trained models over 100B parameters on 400 GPUs at about 15 PetaFLOPs.
extra_html:
How it works

Rather than replicating the model's training state everywhere, ZeRO splits the optimizer states, gradients, and parameters across the data-parallel workers, so each GPU holds only its share. That removes the redundancy that normally caps model size, and the workers exchange what they need during training.

Why it matters

The authors report an 8x increase in trainable model size and a 10x performance jump over the prior state of the art, and ZeRO can run up to 13B-parameter models without any model parallelism at all. It powered the 17B-parameter Turing-NLG and is the engine inside Microsoft's DeepSpeed, making it a widely used way to scale training.

flashcards.prompt: How does ZeRO reduce the memory waste of data-parallel training?

choices.text: It partitions optimizer states, gradients, and parameters across GPUs
It replicates the full training state on every GPU
It splits the weight matrices inside each layer

flashcards.explanation_html: Standard data parallelism replicates the full state on every GPU; ZeRO partitions optimizer states, gradients, and parameters across workers. Splitting in-layer matrices is tensor parallelism.

flashcards.prompt: What does ZeRO's name (Zero Redundancy Optimizer) refer to?
flashcards.back_html: Removing the redundancy of keeping a full copy of the training state on every data-parallel GPU, which normally caps model size.

flashcards.prompt: What scale did the authors report ZeRO could reach without any model parallelism?
flashcards.explanation_html: ZeRO can run up to 13B-parameter models with no model parallelism, and powered the 17B-parameter Turing-NLG.
